title: Fluxboard kernel explorations — weekly notes
content:
Week: 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-24 — Fluxboard kernel explorations
Owner: Asha Patel (notes), primary authors: Marco, Lena, Evan
Context: This week we split the kernel experiments into two threads: 1) lightweight prefetch heuristics that can be toggled at runtime (Fluxboard proto) and 2) micro-batching reorderer changes to make KV shadowing less bursty. The goal is to find low-risk changes we can A/B on canary nodes without touching the hotpath scheduler.

Top-level summary (TL;DR):
- Prefetch heuristic prototype (Fluxboard) reduces cold-token p95 by ~12% on bench workload but increases small-batch latency by ~3% in synthetic spike runs.
- KV shadow writes: introduced a short-window coalesce (50ms) that cuts duplicate writes by ~42% in replay tests; needs safety checks for multi-tenant isolation.
- Batching reorderer tweak (deprioritize very-long-seq requests by score) improved throughput by 4% with no SLA violations on the test fleet.
- Action items: quick rollback guard for prefetch feature flag, add audit for coalesced KV writes, run cross-tenant perf on Dedicated clusters.

Meeting notes and discussion highlights:
- Marco: walked through the Fluxboard heuristic (sketch): combine recent-token entropy signal + prefix-match count to decide prefetch shapes. Prototype implemented as a thin shim before kernel enqueuer. It can be enabled per-node via runtime-config.
  - Observed that for chatlike traces with high prefix reuse, prefetch triggers show good headroom reduction.
  - Edge case: when a long user message follows, prefetch misfires and we create wasted work. Short-term mitigation: add a dampening flag that suppresses prefetch if sequence-length-change delta > X.

- Lena: KV shadow coalesce experiment details.
  - Approach: batch KV-shadow writes that touch identical key buckets within a 50ms window and collapse to a single write with a merged LRU touch vector.
  - Results: benchmark harness (replayed production traces) showed 42% fewer shadow writes, downstream I/O reduced by ~27% on our test nodes.
  - Concerns: correctness when tenants have rapid config flips; we need to ensure we do not delay a critical semantic write. Proposed guard: never coalesce writes for keys in the "session-control" namespace and add an opt-out header for single-tenant Dedicated flows.

- Evan: micro-batching/reorderer changes.
  - Change: add a gentle penalty score for sequences > 8k tokens so they land later in batch formation; keeps most small interactive requests front-and-center.
  - Result: throughput up by ~4% and P99 tail for small requests reduced by ~6ms in lab. No regressions in kernel CPU usage.
  - Note: need to test with streaming workloads since longer-seq deprioritization can interact poorly with streaming start-of-message latency.

Incidental observations / anomalies:
- Canary node OOM on day 2: root cause looks like an unexpected retention in the prefetched KV cache when the dampening flag was temporarily mis-set. Reproduced locally by enabling prefetch without dampening + artificially small eviction window. Fix: hard-limit total prefetch memory per-process to 256MB and emit metric ˆprefetch.overflow_countˆ.
- Load generator showed spike in small-batch latency during KV coalesce runs at ~03:30UTC. Correlated to a background GC sweep on nodes with older kernel builds. Plan: schedule heavy GC + coalesce A/B in isolation, then re-run.

Experiment telemetry snapshot (bench, internal corpus):
- Prefetch (Fluxboard) on canary nodes: cold-token p95 down 12%, cold-token p99 down 6%. Average token cost +1.6% (work added for some traces).
- KV coalesce: shadow-writes -42%, disk-I/O -27%, no error-rate increase (0.02% baseline remains).
- Reorderer: small-request p50 unchanged, small-request p95 down 6ms, throughput +4%.

Risks and mitigations:
- Prefetch overwork risk: mitigated with dampening + memory cap + immediate rollback flag.
- Tenant isolation risk for coalesce: mitigated by namespace exclusions and per-tenant opt-out header. Need legal/ops sign-off before enabling on Dedicated.
- Monitoring gaps: currently we don't have an end-to-end trace tying prefetch decision to end-user perceived latency on production. Action: add trace id propagation from prefetch shim to application-level spans (instrumentation in serving-runtime agent).

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Asha: add a runtime rollback hook that can disable Fluxboard prefetch per-node and wire alert when prefetch.overflow_count > 0. ETA: 2 days.
- Marco: land PR for dampening flag + memory cap (PR: #5983). ETA: 3 days (after code review).
- Lena: add coalesce namespace blacklist and implement an opt-out header. Create Linear ticket for legal/ops review for Dedicated rollout. ETA: 1 week for review ticket.
- Evan: run streaming workload sims against reorderer changes and post results in the thread. ETA: 4 days.
- SRE oncall (assigned): schedule a GC+coalesce isolated test window and verify no small-batch spike. ETA: next maintenance window (4/26).

Open questions (requires cross-team input):
- Product: are we comfortable with a small token-cost increase in exchange for lower p95 cold latency? Which SLA buckets prioritize tail vs cost?
- Security/Compliance: do aggregated KV coalesced writes create any auditability gap for Dedicated customers? (Lena to escalate).
- Observability: what retention window is acceptable for prefetch metrics to ensure we can correlate with user incidents?

Notes to self / low-effort followups: 
- Add a quick dashboard with these metrics: prefetch.trigger_rate, prefetch.overflow_count, coalesce.coalesced_count, reorderer.penalty_hits. Keep 7d retention for rolling lookback.
- Draft short playbook snippet for oncall: how to quickly flip prefetch off and verify node memory returns to baseline.

Appendix: quick experiment run commands (for reproducibility)
- Fluxboard prefetch: ./tools/run_prefetch_bench --dataset=chat-replay --dampening=0.2 --memory-cap-mb=256 --out=flux-run-2026-04-22.csv
- KV coalesce replay: ./tools/replay_kv --trace=prod-replay-2026-03 --coalesce-window-ms=50 --out=coalesce-50ms.json
- Reorderer sim: ./tools/batch_sim --penalty-threshold=8000 --seed=42 --out=reorder-penalty-run.csv

Conversation links and references (informal):
- Slack: #serving-runtime fluxboard thread (link pinned in Linear ticket RW-1423)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5983 (draft)
- Linear: RW-1423, RW-1437

Closing notes: This week felt productive — we have measurable wins and clear guardrails. The emphasis next week is on safety (memory cap + namespace blacklist), more realistic streaming sims, and a small Dedicated-only rollout plan for coalesce once legal signoff is in place.

Unresolved: need a quick decision from Product on tradeoff direction (cost vs tail). I will ping Sahil in Monday sync.

— end of notes (Asha)
